title: Length-synchronous packer: adaptive trimming and runtime-aligned batching
creator: Amina Patel
description: Goals: reduce padding and tail-latency for mixed-length prefill+decode traffic by introducing a length-synchronous packing layer that adapts bucket boundaries at runtime. The packer runs in the request router and produces micro-batches aligned to kernel-preferred sequence lengths and attention-optimization modes. This ticket defines the design, a prototype implementation, perf evaluation, and rollout plan for runtime-aligned adaptive trimming (RAD-Trim).
acceptance_criteria: Prototype integrated with request router and runtime planner (can be toggled by config)
End-to-end e2e test showing >=10% token-cost reduction on mixed-length production trace (internal sim) without increasing 99th percentile latency beyond SLA
Automated fallback to conservative padding when kernel-compatibility constraints prevent packing
Documentation: Confluence design doc + console flag exposed for gradual rollout
Code review and safety checklist completed: PR merged + canary metrics dashboard created
decision_log: 02/12: choose length-synchronous packing (pack by target kernel-friendly sequence lengths) over per-request greedy trimming because it enables deterministic kernel selection and simpler KV cache reuse. 02/20: adopt conservative kernel-compatibility map (kernel signature -> supported sequence length ranges) instead of tight auto-probing to avoid runtime failures. 03/02: enable prefix-coalesce only for prefill requests with identical prompt hash to preserve semantic cache safety.
blockers: Need updated kernel capability matrix from infra (ticket INF-1456)
Model-variant incompatibility for certain attention optimizations: awaiting research verification
comments: 2026-02-10 Amina Patel: Initial spike completed. Implemented a simple prototype in the router that buckets by 8/16/32/64 sequence lengths and applies greedy trim to prefill sequences. Observed 7–9% token reduction on sampled beta workload; breakdown shows most wins on 16–48 token queries.

2026-02-14 Diego Rivera: Prototype updated to emit kernel_signature hints to the planner. This lets the runtime pick attention kernels optimized for short vs long sequences. Implemented a compatibility map to avoid selecting kernels that don't support KV prefill reuse. Patch: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4523.

2026-02-18 Sophie Chen (Research): Ran attention-mode microbenchmarks. Short-seq specialized kernels (fused QK + masked-softmax) give 12–18% throughput on <64 seq; but memory layout expectations require 16-byte alignment. Added alignment-aware target lengths to packing logic.
2026-02-25 PM review (Ravi Kapoor): Asked for clear rollback criteria. Added canary gating: enable only when token-cost improvement >=8% and 99p latency delta <= +5ms for the canary cohort.

2026-03-01 Diego Rivera: Integration test failures surfaced when rolling for multi-tenant Dedicated clusters — issue was stale kernel capability cache on agent. Added a lease-based capability refresh and fallback path that disables RAD-Trim for that node.

2026-03-08 QA (Marta Ivanov): Canary run (prod-sim) for 48h: token cost down 11.3% on mixed-search workload, median latency improved by 6%, 99p increased 3.2ms (within allowed). Noted 0.03% of requests hit fallback due to kernel incompatibility — logged as INF-1522.

2026-03-10 Diego Rivera: Preparing rollout playbook. Tasks left: finalize console toggle (console PR ready), add audit log entries for pack decisions, and schedule Dedicated canary. target rollout week 2026-W14.
